arguments.summary: A credential compromise incident was initiated by an external IP (91.219.236.174) targeting user 'j.martinez'. The attacker performed reconnaissance via a network scan, gained access using compromised credentials, and successfully authenticated to internal systems. No malware was detected on the initial host, but the risk of credential harvesting led to the revocation of the compromised account and expansion of access revocation across lateral and departmental accounts. The attacker's IP has been blocked at the firewall.

Firewall rule implemented to block inbound traffic from 91.219.236.174.

arguments.summary: A supply chain compromise was initiated via a phishing email to user CORP\jsmith, leading to the execution of an encoded PowerShell command from Outlook. This launched a malicious DLL ('beacon.dll') via rundll32.exe from the Temp directory, establishing a C2 beacon to 198.51.100.23 over HTTPS. The attacker modified the local hosts file for persistence and performed lateral movement using compromised service accounts (svc-backup, svc-sql-prod, admin-deploy, svc-monitoring). The incident affected 200 production servers. Containment actions included revocation of four critical service accounts and execution of an Ansible playbook to rotate all local credentials across the production environment.
